name: Build Courses
before:
The previous step's result gives you the ENTRÉES for Day {{slot.day}}, each declaring the diets it feeds. For each of those slots, write the dishes that accompany that entrée — never the entrée itself, which already exists.

THIS IS DAY {{slot.day}} OF A {{days}}-DAY CYCLE, for the {{slot.diet}} diet. EVERY ACCOMPANIMENT IS CHOSEN FOR THE ENTRÉE PRINTED ABOVE, and that entrée is different on every day of the cycle — so this day's accompaniments are different too. Read the entrée's own ingredients first: a side that repeats the starch or the vegetable already cooked into the entrée is the same food twice on one tray, and the same side written on every day of the cycle is the defect this step exists to prevent.

{{#if pairingMethodology}}Choose each accompaniment for flavor affinity with the entrée using this approach: {{pairingMethodology}}.{{/if}}
{{#if courseList}}This meal offers these course positions: {{courseList}}. The ENTRÉE positions in that list are ALREADY WRITTEN by the previous step — never write a row for them. For every OTHER position on that list, write AT LEAST ONE row. More than one is allowed and often better; there is no upper limit. What is NOT allowed is a position on that list with no row at all, or a row for a position the list never named.{{else}}No course list was given, so write SIDES ONLY — at least one `side` row per slot. Do not invent soup, salad, dessert, drink, appetizer, starch or vegetable positions that were not asked for.{{/if}}

A SAUCE IS NEVER A DISH ON ITS OWN. Never give a sauce, gravy, dressing, dip, relish or condiment a row to itself — it has no Kind it can legally take. It arrives as PART OF A DISH: the dish is `Mashed Potatoes and Gravy`, not a `Gravy` row beside a `Mashed Potatoes` row. Write that one dish, and name the sauce in its Components as `<sauce>:seasoning`.

MEALTIME is the SERVICE PERIOD the dish is served in — WHEN the tray goes out. Its only legal values are this plan's own mealtimes: {{join meals ", "}}. Copy one of those, spelled exactly as written there, and write nothing else in that column. Every row on this call carries the mealtime of the slot it belongs to.
MEALTIME AND KIND ARE INDEPENDENT: Mealtime is WHEN it is served, Kind is WHAT POSITION it fills on the tray. One does not decide the other. A word can sit on both lists — `dessert` is the clearest case:
  - `dessert` as MEALTIME = the service period when the tray goes out (a dessert service period).
  - `dessert` as KIND = the course position on the tray (a dessert course served during the lunch mealtime).
So a dessert-Kind row is normally served at lunch or dinner, NOT at a mealtime called dessert; writing `dessert` in Mealtime just because Kind is `dessert` is a defect. Check the Mealtime cell against this plan's mealtime list and the Kind cell against the Kind list; a value that is not on the list for THAT column is a defect, even when it is on the other one.
KIND is the COURSE POSITION the dish occupies on the tray — what it IS to the diner, not what it is made of. {{#if (without (keys courseCounts) "entree")}}The course positions for this call are: {{join (without (keys courseCounts) "entree") ", "}}.
Kind is one of those positions. Never `entree`. No other value may appear in that column.{{else}}Kind is never `entree`.{{/if}}
DIETS lists which diets the dish is SAFE for. Every value in that cell must be copied exactly from this plan's diet list: {{join diets ", "}}. Separate several with a comma. WRITE NOTHING ELSE IN THAT CELL — never a diet that is not on that list, never the word NOT, never a negation, never a reason, never a parenthesis. `NOT vegetarian` and `standard (no nuts)` are both defects; `{{join diets ", "}}` is the shape. If the dish is unsafe for every diet on the list, do not write the dish at all.
Diets SHARE these dishes: write one row that feeds them all wherever possible, and a separate row only where a diet cannot have it.
Fill only the component columns the dish actually occupies; leave the others empty.

Output ONLY pipe-delimited rows, one per line, with this header and nothing else, UNLESS you are specifically instructed to overload it:
Day | Mealtime | Dish | Protein | Starch | Vegetable | Fruit | Kind | Diets | Components
